mainTopic: Whether we rely on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו for Torah laws, and the גמרא's analysis of the figs ברייתא
overview: This amud continues the מחלוקת between רב נחמן and רב ששת about relying on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו, the presumption that a messenger did his job. רב נחמן says we rely on it only for rabbinic laws, like עירוב. רב ששת says we rely on it for Torah laws too. רב ששת brings three proofs: the עומר and חדש, the woman who puts money for her קרבנות in the שופר box, and a ברייתא about picking figs from a friend's tree. רב נחמן answers each one the same way: the trust there comes from someone especially reliable, such as the בית דין, the court of כהנים, or a חבר, and not from the general rule about messengers. The גמרא then goes back to the figs ברייתא to understand it on its own terms. It asks to whom the עם הארץ owner is speaking, and why the סיפא mentions feeding טבל to an עם הארץ. רבינא answers that the רישא and the סיפא describe different cases, and the explanation of רבי's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן: For rabbinic laws we trust the messenger
steps.stepSummary: The second half of רב נחמן's statement: for rabbinic laws, we assume a messenger did what he was sent to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: For rabbinic laws, there is a presumption that a messenger carries out his mission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's ruling, which started on the previous amud: for Torah laws we do not trust that the messenger did his job, but for rabbinic laws we do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full statement is a split: Torah law requires certainty, so we cannot rely on the assumption that a שליח did his job. Rabbinic law is more lenient, so the assumption is enough. This matters for our case, because עירוב is a rabbinic law, so we may rely on the messenger who was sent to place it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic law (literally 'of the scribes')
A presumption; something we may assume is true without checking
A messenger or agent
His mission or errand

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the second half of רב נחמן's statement. The first half, which appears on the previous amud, says that for Torah laws (של תורה) we do NOT rely on this presumption.

phrases.english: With regard to rabbinic laws —
phrases.notes: This is the other half of the rule. The first half, about Torah laws (בשל תורה), was on the previous amud.

phrases.english: there is a presumption that a messenger does his mission.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁל סוֹפְרִים חֲזָקָה שָׁלִיחַ עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן's two-part ruling, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For rabbinic laws, we rely on the presumption that a messenger fulfilled his mission. For Torah laws, we do not.

steps.title: רב ששת: We trust the messenger for both kinds of law
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת disagrees and says the presumption applies to Torah laws and rabbinic laws alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: For both this and that, there is a presumption that a messenger carries out his mission.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת argues with רב נחמן. He says we may trust that the messenger did his job even for Torah laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This and that' means Torah law and rabbinic law. For רב ששת, the presumption is strong enough to rely on even where the Torah requires certainty. This sets up a clear מחלוקת that the next steps will test.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; the same rule for both cases

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Both this and that —
phrases.notes: Both Torah law and rabbinic law.

phrases.english: there is a presumption that a messenger does his mission.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן by extending the presumption to Torah laws.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The presumption that a messenger fulfills his mission applies to Torah laws and rabbinic laws alike.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes the משנה about new grain and the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת cites a משנה: once the עומר is brought, new grain is permitted, and people far away may eat it from midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: From where do I learn this? As we learned in a משנה: Once the עומר has been offered, the new grain is permitted right away. And those who live far away are permitted from midday onward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is setting up a proof for his view by quoting a משנה. The next step will explain how this משנה proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids eating new grain (חדש) until the עומר offering is brought on the 16th of ניסן. People in ירושלים can see when it is brought. People far away cannot see it, yet the משנה still lets them eat from midday, because by then it was surely brought.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (The speaker introduces a proof for his own view.)
As we learned in a משנה
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
New grain, forbidden until the עומר is offered
Those who live far away from ירושלים
Midday

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
From where do I say this? As we learned in a Mishnah:
Once the Omer has been offered,
the new grain is permitted immediately.
And those far away are permitted
phrases.notes: They cannot see when the עומר is brought.

phrases.english: from midday and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ששת begins to support his own position with a source.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that the presumption applies even to Torah laws.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מנחות about the עומר and חדש.

steps.title: Why the משנה proves the presumption works for Torah law
steps.stepSummary: חדש is a Torah prohibition, yet far-away people rely on the כהנים having brought the עומר. So the presumption works for Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But חדש is a Torah law, and still the משנה teaches that those far away may eat from midday. Isn't that because of the presumption that a messenger carries out his mission?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת draws the conclusion from the משנה: we see the presumption being used for a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים in the בית המקדש act as messengers for all of כלל ישראל in bringing the עומר. Far-away people never check that the עומר was offered, yet they may eat Torah-forbidden חדש by midday. The only reason must be that we trust the messengers did their job, against רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah; a Torah-level law
And yet it teaches
Is it not because...? (A rhetorical question that pushes a conclusion.)

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, רב נחמן's distinction between Torah and rabbinic law falls apart.

phrases.english: But the new grain prohibition is a Torah law,
and yet it teaches: those far away are permitted
from midday and onward.
Is it not because of the presumption
that a messenger does his mission?
phrases.notes: The כהנים are the messengers of the whole nation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic of the proof from the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the presumption a messenger fulfills his mission applies even to Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Far-away people may eat חדש from midday without knowing for sure that the עומר was brought.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The court is a special case
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה itself gives the reason: the בית דין is never lazy about the עומר. So this does not prove anything about ordinary messengers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רב נחמן answer this? There, it is because of the reason the משנה itself states: because people know that the court is not lazy about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן deals with the proof, then answers for him: the עומר case has its own special reason, so it says nothing about ordinary messengers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not deny that the far-away people may eat. He says their reliance is not based on the general presumption about messengers. It is based on a special certainty: the בית דין is never careless about the עומר. An ordinary messenger, like one sent to place an עירוב, gets no such guarantee.

keyTerms.meaning: There; in that other case
As the reason is taught; the source itself gives the reason
The court; here, the authorities responsible for the עומר
Lazy or negligent

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: we trust a messenger only for rabbinic law. רב ששת: we trust a messenger for both kinds of law. רב ששת's proof from the עומר is pushed off, because the בית דין is specially reliable, which ordinary messengers are not.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the far-away people are wrong to eat. He agrees they may eat. He only disagrees about WHY: the reason is the reliability of the בית דין, not the general rule about messengers.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman (how does he answer)?
There, it is as the reason is taught —
phrases.notes: The reason is stated in the משנה itself.

phrases.english: because they know
that the court is not lazy about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב נחמן by pushing off רב ששת's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not disprove רב ששת's view, but shows the משנה is no evidence for it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that the far-away people rely on the general messenger presumption. In fact, the משנה explicitly bases their reliance on the special diligence of the בית דין, which does not apply to ordinary messengers.

steps.title: Second version: רב נחמן uses the עומר משנה as his own proof
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב נחמן says the עומר משנה actually proves his view. The משנה stresses that the בית דין is not lazy, which implies an ordinary שליח might be lazy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: רב נחמן said, 'Where do I get my view from? The משנה gives a reason: because people know the בית דין is not lazy about it. So it is the בית דין that is not lazy. That means an ordinary messenger might be lazy!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב נחמן's response. Here he is not just defending himself. He goes on the attack and uses the same משנה to prove his own position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 5), רב נחמן only showed that the משנה does not prove רב ששת's view. Here he reads it more strongly. The משנה needed to point out the special reliability of the בית דין, so an ordinary שליח must not be reliable enough for a Torah law. The extra reason in the משנה becomes a דיוק (inference) supporting him.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces a second version of the same discussion
From where do I say this? (introduces a proof for one's own view)
Are lazy / slow to act
But this implies…: used to draw an inference from what was said

steps.confusionAlert: This is the SAME משנה from Steps 3–5, not a new source. The difference is only in how רב נחמן uses it. In the first version he deflects it, and in this version he uses it as a proof.

phrases.english: And some say (a different version):

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: From where do I say this?
Because it teaches the reason:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁיּוֹדְעִין שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מִתְעַצְּלִין בּוֹ.
phrases.english: because they know that the court is not lazy about it.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה about the עומר.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין הוּא דְּלָא מִתְעַצְּלִין בּוֹ —
phrases.english: It is the court that is not lazy about it —
which implies that a messenger may be lazy about it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of Step 5. The deflection is upgraded into a positive proof for רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that the presumption does not apply to Torah laws when an ordinary שליח is involved.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's stated reason about the עומר: 'because they know the בית דין is not lazy about it.'

steps.title: רב ששת reads the same משנה as being about timing only
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the difference between a בית דין and a שליח is only about how fast they work. The בית דין finishes by midday, and a שליח finishes by the end of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת can say to you: the court is trusted to finish by midday, while a messenger is trusted to finish by the end of the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב ששת would push back on רב נחמן's inference from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת agrees that the משנה contrasts a בית דין with a שליח, but he says the contrast is about speed, not trust. A בית דין is so diligent that you can rely on it already from midday. An ordinary שליח can also be relied on, just not until the day is over. So the presumption still works for Torah laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Can say to you: introduces how the other side would answer
The middle of the day (midday)
The whole day

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is NOT admitting that a שליח is untrustworthy. He holds that a שליח is fully trusted, just with a later deadline than a בית דין.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet can say to you:
The court is presumed done by midday,
a messenger by the end of the whole day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב נחמן's inference in Step 6 by giving a different reading of the contrast in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that a שליח cannot be relied on at all. It leaves the משנה itself intact.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן assumed the contrast was about whether we can rely on someone. It can just as well be about how quickly we can rely on them.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof from the woman who puts money in the collection box
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא. A woman who owes קרבנות after לידה or זיבה puts money in the שופר box, immerses, and eats קדשים that evening. She must be relying on the presumption that the messenger did his job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Where do I get my view from? A ברייתא teaches: A woman who must bring offerings after giving birth or after זיבה brings money and puts it into the collection box. Then she immerses and eats sacred food that evening. What is the reason? Is it not because we say there is a presumption that a messenger carries out his mission?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a new source, a ברייתא, to prove that the presumption works even for Torah-level matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a woman may not eat קדשים until her קרבנות are offered, and that is a Torah requirement. She never sees the כהנים buy and offer her birds, yet she eats that night. That only makes sense if we presume the messengers did their job, even for a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Childbirth, after which a woman brings קרבנות
A זבה's condition (abnormal flow), after which she brings קרבנות
Here: a horn-shaped collection box in the בית המקדש
Sacred sacrificial food
The presumption that a messenger carries out his mission

steps.confusionAlert: The word שופר here does NOT mean a ram's horn for blowing. It is a collection box shaped like a horn.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ לֵידָה אוֹ זִיבָה,
phrases.english: A woman who owes offerings for childbirth or zivah
brings money and puts it in the collection box,
immerses, and eats sacred food in the evening.
What is the reason?
Is it not because we say
there is a presumption that a messenger carries out his mission?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending his reading of the עומר משנה, רב ששת brings a new, independent source for his view.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו applies even to Torah laws.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a woman after לידה or זיבה who relies on her money in the שופר being used for her קרבנות.

steps.title: רב נחמן answers: the priests' court never leaves until all the money is used
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the woman relies on a special בית דין of כהנים. רב שמעיה taught that this court does not leave until all the money in the box has been spent. That tells us nothing about an ordinary שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רב נחמן answer? There, it follows רב שמעיה, who said: There is a presumption that the court of כהנים does not leave until all the money in the collection box has been used up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן would deal with רב ששת's proof, and answers by quoting רב שמעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן uses the same move as with the עומר. The case involves a special court whose job is to finish the task, not an ordinary messenger. Since the trust comes from the court's diligence, the ברייתא does not prove that an ordinary שליח is trusted for Torah laws.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that case)
An אמורא whose teaching about the כהנים' court is quoted
The court of כהנים in charge of the Temple funds and offerings
Until they use up (finish)

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רב ששת's proofs (the עומר and the woman's קרבנות) involve a בית דין. רב נחמן answers both the same way: a בית דין is especially diligent, so we cannot learn from it about an ordinary שליח for Torah laws.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman (how does he answer)?
There, it is like Rav Shemaya's teaching,
for Rav Shemaya said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה אֵין בֵּית דִּין שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: There is a presumption that the court of priests does not
get up and leave from there
until they have used up all the money in the collection box.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's proof in Step 8, using the same reasoning רב נחמן used for the עומר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא as proof about ordinary messengers. The ברייתא's ruling itself stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The woman's reliance comes from the special diligence of the כהנים' court, not from the general presumption about messengers.

steps.title: A source about picking figs from a friend's tree
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא. If an owner tells a friend to pick figs with no set amount, the friend must tithe them as definitely untithed (ודאי). If the owner says 'fill this basket,' the friend tithes them only as a doubt (דמאי).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: How do I know this? A ברייתא teaches: If a man tells his friend, 'Go pick yourself figs from my fig tree,' the friend may eat a casual snack from them, but he must tithe them as fruit that was surely never tithed. If the man said, 'Fill this basket for yourself with figs from my fig tree,' the friend may eat a casual snack, and he must tithe them as דמאי (fruit that maybe was tithed and maybe was not).
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת opens a new proof for his view by quoting the first part of a ברייתא about figs. This step sets up the proof. The actual inference is drawn in Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'go pick' case, the owner has no idea how many figs will be taken, so he could not have tithed for them. That is why they count as surely untithed (ודאי). In the 'fill this basket' case, the owner knows the amount, so maybe he already tithed for them from other fruit. That doubt makes them דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (How do I know this?)
A casual snack, not a fixed meal. Untithed fruit may be eaten this way.
Certainly. Here: fruit that was surely never tithed.
Fruit we are unsure was tithed. It is tithed in a lighter way.
A basket

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cases apart. 'Go pick' means the owner does not know the amount, so the fruit is surely untithed (ודאי). 'Fill this basket' means the owner knows the amount, so he may have tithed it already (דמאי).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught in a baraita: One who says to his friend:
'Go and gather for yourself figs from my fig tree'
he may eat from them casually
and he must tithe them as certainly untithed.
phrases.notes: The owner did not know the amount, so he could not have tithed for them.

phrases.english: 'Fill this basket for yourself'
'with figs from my fig tree'
he may eat from them casually
and he must tithe them as demai.
phrases.notes: The owner knew the amount, so he may already have tithed for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן pushed away רב ששת's earlier proof about the שופר box, so רב ששת now brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that we may rely on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about picking figs from a friend's tree

steps.title: רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about an owner who is a חבר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The 'basket' rule applies when the owner is an עם הארץ. If the owner is a חבר, רבי says the picker does not need to tithe at all. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he must tithe, because a חבר does not tithe from fruit that is not next to the fruit being exempted.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the owner is an עם הארץ. But if he is a חבר, the picker may eat without tithing at all. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: When is this said? When the owner is an עם הארץ. But if he is a חבר, the picker may not eat until he tithes, because חברים are not suspected of separating תרומה from fruit that is not next to the fruit it exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with an argument between רבי and his father, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, about an owner who is a careful חבר. The proof is still being built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a חבר surely tithed for the figs in the basket from his other fruit, so the picker can rely on him. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a חבר would not tithe from fruit that is not next to these figs (מוקף). So the owner did not tithe them, and the picker must do it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (This limits the rule just taught.)
A person who is not careful about tithes and purity
A person known to be careful about tithes and purity
Fruit lying right next to the fruit it is meant to exempt. Ideally, tithes are separated from fruit that is next to it.
To separate תרומה (and tithes)

phrases.english: In what case is this said? With an am ha'aretz.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּחָבֵר — אוֹכֵל וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְעַשֵּׂר,
phrases.english: But with a ḥaver, he may eat and need not tithe,
phrases.notes: The owner surely tithed for these figs from his other produce.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
In what case is this said? With an am ha'aretz.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּחָבֵר — אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל עַד שֶׁיְּעַשֵּׂר,
phrases.english: But with a ḥaver, he may not eat until he tithes,
because ḥaverim are not suspected
of separating teruma from produce that is not adjacent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the same ברייתא and limits its rule to an owner who is an עם הארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner is a חבר, רבי says the picker need not tithe. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he must tithe, because a חבר does not tithe from fruit that is not מוקף.

steps.title: רבי explains why he disagrees with his father
steps.stepSummary: רבי says his view is more reasonable. It is better for a חבר to tithe from fruit that is not next to it than to let an עם הארץ end up eating untithed fruit (טבל).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: My words seem better than my father's words. It is better that חברים should tithe from fruit that is not next to it, than that they should feed עמי הארץ untithed fruit (טבל).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his reason for disagreeing with his father. This is still part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees that tithing from fruit that is not next to it (שלא מן המוקף) is not ideal. But a חבר would rather do that than be the cause of someone else eating טבל. So a חבר surely tithed for the basket from his other fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: My words seem correct (more reasonable)
It is better
Untithed produce (טבל), which may not be eaten

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דְּבָרַי מִדִּבְרֵי אַבָּא.
phrases.english: Rabbi said: My words appear more correct than Father's words.
It is better that ḥaverim should be suspected
of separating teruma from produce that is not adjacent,
and that they should not feed amei ha'aretz untithed produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דְּבָרַי מִדִּבְרֵי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי gives the reason for the view he stated in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חבר would rather tithe from fruit that is not next to it than cause others to eat טבל.

steps.title: Everyone agrees that a messenger does his job
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the proof. רבי and his father argue only about whether a חבר would tithe from fruit that is not next to it. Both agree that we rely on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue about this point: one Sage holds that חברים are suspected of tithing from fruit that is not next to it, and the other Sage holds they are not. But everyone agrees: there is a presumption that a messenger does his job.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב ששת's proof. It shows that both sides of the ברייתא accept the rule that a messenger can be trusted to do his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner acts like a messenger who must tithe so that nobody eats טבל because of him. The two Sages argue only about whether a חבר would tithe from fruit that is not next to it (מוקף). Neither one suggests the owner might simply neglect his job of tithing, so both accept חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו, which is רב ששת's view.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue up to here (this is the only point of argument)
One Sage holds
Everyone agrees
There is a presumption that a messenger does his job

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's final proof: even רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who argue about מוקף, both agree on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the main question of the sugya. It decides whether someone may rely on a messenger who was sent to place his עירוב.

phrases.english: They disagree only
in that one Sage holds: they are suspected,
and one Sage holds: they are not suspected.
phrases.notes: This second Sage is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: But everyone agrees:
there is a presumption that an agent fulfills his agency.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא דְּמָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא draws the inference from the ברייתא that was quoted in steps 10 through 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's view that we rely on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only about מוקף, so both accept that the owner did his job of tithing.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the trust comes from a rule about a חבר, not about agents
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן deflects the proof. In the figs case, we trust the חבר because of רב חנינא חוזאה's חזקה: a חבר never lets untithed food leave his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן answers: there, the case follows רב חנינא חוזאה. רב חנינא חוזאה said that we can presume a חבר will not let anything untithed leave his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back against the proof from Step 13. He says the figs case does not depend on trusting a שליח at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 claimed that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל both rely on חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו. רב נחמן gives a different reason for the case. We trust the owner because he is a חבר, and a חבר never gives out untithed food. Since the trust comes from the person's status, the ברייתא proves nothing about agents in general.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal presumption that we rely on without checking
A person known to be careful about tithes and purity laws
Fixed up, meaning properly tithed
רב חנינא from the region of Chozai, an אמורא

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן escapes the proof. The trust in the figs case comes from a חזקה about every חבר, not from a חזקה about agents.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the main debate about חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו for now. The rest of the sugya turns to explaining the ברייתא itself.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman [would answer]:
phrases.notes: Now we hear how רב נחמן would answer רב ששת's proof.

phrases.english: there, it is like Rav Chanina Chozaah
for Rav Chanina Chozaah said:
It is a presumption about a chaver
that he does not release anything that is not tithed
from under his hand (from his possession).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן, הָתָם כִּדְרַב חֲנִינָא חוֹזָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Deflects the proof drawn in Step 13 by giving another reason for the ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the figs ברייתא proves חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The trust in the figs case comes from a חזקה about a חבר's personal habits, not from a חזקה about agents.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again to study it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes part of the figs ברייתא. If the owner is a חבר, the picker eats without tithing, according to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: When does this rule apply? When the owner is an עם הארץ. But if the owner is a חבר, the picker may eat and does not need to tithe. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can ask questions about it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The debate about agents is finished. Now the גמרא wants to understand the ברייתא on its own terms. The phrase אמר מר signals that a line from a source just quoted is being brought back for close study.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said": the formula for re-quoting a source to analyze it
"In what case were these words said?": limits a rule to a specific case
A person not trusted to be careful about tithes

phrases.english: The Master said:
In what case are these words said? With an am ha'aretz,
but with a chaver,
he eats and does not need to tithe,
these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the agency debate and re-quotes the ברייתא to analyze its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the owner is an עם הארץ, the picker tithes as דמאי. If the owner is a חבר, רבי says the picker eats without tithing.

steps.title: Who is the עם הארץ owner speaking to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the picker is. If he is another עם הארץ, the ברייתא's instruction to tithe as דמאי makes no sense, because he would not obey it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This עם הארץ owner, whom is he talking to? If you say he is talking to his fellow עם הארץ, then how can the ברייתא say "he tithes them as דמאי"? Would that person listen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the picker in the ברייתא is. It immediately rules out one option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells the picker to tithe the figs as דמאי. An עם הארץ does not follow the rules of דמאי, so a ruling aimed at him would be pointless. The picker must be someone who actually keeps these rules.

keyTerms.meaning: To whom?
"If you say": introduces a possible answer that will be rejected
"Would he obey?": a rhetorical question meaning he would not
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, tithed only out of doubt

phrases.aramaic: הַאי עַם הָאָרֶץ, דְּקָאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְמַאן?
phrases.english: This am ha'aretz, to whom is he saying it?
If you say that he says it to his fellow am ha'aretz,
[then the ruling] "he tithes them as demai": would he obey?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי עַם הָאָרֶץ, דְּקָאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא that was just re-quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the picker whom the עם הארץ owner is addressing.

steps.title: The picker must be a חבר
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the עם הארץ owner is speaking to a חבר, who will obey the rules of דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is an עם הארץ who tells a חבר to pick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The picker is a חבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a חבר would follow an instruction to tithe as דמאי, so he must be the picker. This answer seems to fit the רישא. The next step tests whether it also fits the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: "Rather": introduces the corrected answer

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ דְּקָאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחָבֵר.
phrases.english: Rather, [it is] an am ha'aretz who says it to a chaver.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ דְּקָאֲמַר לֵיהּ לְחָבֵר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner is an עם הארץ and the picker is a חבר.

steps.title: The סיפא mentions feeding an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא worries about a חבר feeding טבל to an עם הארץ. If the picker is a חבר, there is no עם הארץ eating anything, so why does the סיפא mention one?
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the סיפא: "My words seem more reasonable than my father's. Better that חברים be suspected of tithing from fruit that is not next to it than that they feed טבל to עמי הארץ." What is an עם הארץ doing there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 17 using the סיפא of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an עם הארץ owner is speaking to a חבר picker, the one eating the figs is a חבר. Yet in the סיפא, רבי's reasoning is about not feeding טבל to an עם הארץ. So the סיפא seems to describe a case where an עם הארץ is the one eating, which does not match.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say the latter clause": the latter part of the source will now be used to test the reading
Fruit that is next to the fruit being tithed
Untithed produce, forbidden to eat
"What is it doing there?": this detail does not fit the case

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
My words appear [more correct] than my father's words,
it is better that chaverim be suspected
of separating tithes from what is not adjacent
and not feed amei ha'aretz untithed produce.
What are amei ha'aretz doing there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: נִרְאִין דְּבָרַי מִדִּבְרֵי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 17 using the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the whole ברייתא is about an עם הארץ owner speaking to a חבר picker.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that case no עם הארץ eats the fruit. Yet the סיפא's reasoning is about not feeding טבל to עמי הארץ.

steps.title: רבינא: the two clauses describe different cases
steps.stepSummary: רבינא splits the ברייתא. The רישא is an עם הארץ telling a חבר to pick. The סיפא is a חבר owner telling an עם הארץ to pick, while another חבר overhears.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The רישא is an עם הארץ speaking to a חבר. The סיפא is a חבר speaking to an עם הארץ, while another חבר hears him. רבי...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by saying the רישא and the סיפא describe different cases. This passage ends just as the גמרא begins to explain רבי's view under this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the owner is a חבר and the picker is an עם הארץ. That explains why the סיפא talks about feeding an עם הארץ. A second חבר who overheard the instruction is the one asking whether he may eat the figs. The רישא keeps the reading from Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא
The first clause of a source
The latter clause of a source
Hears him

steps.confusionAlert: In the סיפא, the one whose eating is in question is the second חבר who overheard. It is not the עם הארץ who was told to pick.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
The first clause: with an am ha'aretz who said it to a chaver,
the latter clause: with a chaver who said it to an am ha'aretz,
and another chaver hears him.
Rabbi...
phrases.notes: This sentence carries on to the next amud, where we see how רבי's view works the way רבינא reads it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: רֵישָׁא בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁאָמַר לְחָבֵר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the רישא and the סיפא describe different scenarios.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses describe one case, an עם הארץ owner speaking to a חבר picker.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is an עם הארץ telling a חבר. The סיפא is a חבר telling an עם הארץ, with a second חבר overhearing.
